content.value_statement: Agent files can fail when triggers, frontmatter, or prompts are vague. This skill gives structured patterns, examples, and validation steps for production agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code agent markdown structure and required YAML frontmatter fields.
Provides trigger description patterns with concrete example blocks and commentary.
Guides system prompt design for roles, responsibilities, workflows, and output formats.
Documents model, color, and tool access choices for agent configuration.
Includes complete sample agents for review, testing, documentation, and security analysis.
Includes a Bash validator for checking agent file structure and common field issues.
limitations: It does not run or host agents by itself.
It targets Claude Code plugin agents, not every agent framework.
Generated agents still need project-specific review and testing.
The validator checks structure and simple patterns, not full behavioral quality.

use_cases.title: Create a Plugin Agent
use_cases.description: Define a new Claude Code agent with valid frontmatter, scoped tools, and a clear system prompt.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Triggering
use_cases.description: Rewrite descriptions and examples so Claude selects the right agent at the right time.

use_cases.title: Validate Agent Files
use_cases.description: Check agent markdown files for required fields, naming rules, prompt presence, and common warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code agent for this task: [task]. Include name, description examples, model, color, tools, and system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Trigger Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve when an agent is selected
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description and improve the triggering examples. Make each example include context, user request, assistant response, and commentary.

prompt_templates.title: Limit Tool Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this agent purpose, recommend the minimum Claude Code tools it needs. Explain why each tool is needed and which tools to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Agent Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this complete agent file for frontmatter validity, trigger precision, prompt completeness, tool scope, edge cases, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews pull requests for quality and security issues.
output_examples.output: A proposed agent name, trigger description with examples, scoped read-only tools, and a reviewer system prompt.

output_examples.input: Validate this agent file before I add it to a plugin.
output_examples.output: A checklist of required fields, naming issues, prompt length concerns, tool scope warnings, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Make this agent trigger only after code is written, not during planning.
output_examples.output: Revised trigger examples that distinguish completed implementation work from planning or discussion requests.

best_practices: Use specific trigger examples that show when to invoke the agent and when not to invoke it.
Grant only the tools required for the agent purpose and expected workflow.
Test each agent with realistic requests before publishing it in a plugin.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic names or descriptions that could match many unrelated requests.
Do not omit output format guidance from the agent system prompt.
Do not grant full tool access unless the agent truly needs it.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code plugin agents with valid structure, clear triggers, scoped tools, and useful system prompts.

faq.question: Does it create agents automatically?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance. You still review the output and save the agent file in your plugin.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to help design, review, and validate Claude Code agent files.

faq.question: Why are trigger examples important?
faq.answer: Trigger examples teach when the agent should be selected and reduce accidental invocation for unrelated tasks.

faq.question: How should I choose tools for an agent?
faq.answer: Start with the smallest useful tool set. Add write or shell access only when the workflow requires it.

faq.question: What should I validate before publishing?
faq.answer: Check required frontmatter, name format, description examples, prompt length, output format, and tool permissions.
